Dear Livia-Cristina,

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 23 July 2025. Please find our response to your requests below.

*Suspicious activity detected on your account*

We note that your request focuses on the restriction of access to your Bolt driver account. This was the result of *failed Identification verification.* Bolt requires drivers to successfully complete identity verification in accordance with platform security standards and applicable regulations. This verification process is essential to ensure that only authorized individuals operate under valid driver profiles.Your account was suspended due to irregularities identified during the identity verification process. In particular, the information we received appeared to come from different locations in a way that didn’t match what we’d expect from a single person completing the process. To keep the platform safe and fair for everyone, we couldn’t complete your verification at this time.

*_Information on automated decision-making_*

Bolt may use automated processes for certain processing activities, including fraud detection and prevention, trip allocation, and price setting. In each case, these processes either involve human review or do not result in decisions that have a significant impact on drivers’ rights or opportunities. For further details we refer you to our [Driver Privacy Notice|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/privacy/].

*Data access request*

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled, including state logs and verifications.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy. If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely, 

*Bolt*

Hey, [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] - since we’d prefer to send out the response by the end of this week, I would appreciate receiving your guidance in the upcoming days. In that legal response (that will be more of a formal letter signed by Samantha), we would like to specify in a non-binding way what actions we have undertaken to improve our processes. I have not much to add apart from what has been said already above, but I am pasting here the summary of the whole case:



# *What happened* 

Sarah took a ride with an allegedly-installed CCTV device installed in it, and had not been informed about it prior to the ride. We have already been through several rounds of communication exchanges with her. After multiple rounds of communication, she has finally requested:

* *Full Refund* – Confirmation that all three rides will be refunded, as Hopp originally promised (not just the partial $37 refund).
* *Explanation* – A clear explanation of why Hopp’s refund handling has changed multiple times.
* *Case Removal Clarification* – An immediate explanation of why one of her open refund cases disappeared from her account history.
* *Current Refund Status* – Confirmation of the present status of the refund for all three rides.

The details on those 3 rides are here:

# *Order 586375540*: The driver’s photo didn’t match; she requested a full refund, threatened to go to authorities, rejected a $5 credit, and insists on refunds for all three cases.
# *Order 588814983*: The car had CCTV and stickers that were hard to notice, with no app or in-car warning; she demanded a full refund and mentioned authorities.
# *Order 586695687*: Another CCTV case (allegedly without stickers) where a refund was offered, but she refused unless all three orders are refunded together.

Our response to the following mostly relied on saying that:

*Driver Responsibility:*
Our response emphasised that Hopp does not install, operate, or control in-vehicle CCTV equipment. Drivers on the platform are independent contractors and, in this context, act as the data controllers for any recordings they choose to make. Under PIPEDA, Hopp as a company is only responsible for personal information that it collects, uses, or discloses. Since Hopp does not receive, access, or process any CCTV recordings, the responsibility for compliance with privacy obligations lies solely with the driver.

*Guidance to Drivers:*
We highlighted that Hopp has issued [+_guidance_+|https://gethopp.com/en/support/articles/94056/] to drivers regarding the use of cameras.

*Goodwill Refunds:*
As a gesture of goodwill, and without admission of liability, we offered refunds for the rides in question. However, the refund handling became inconsistent across different support tiers, creating additional frustration and mistrust.

# *Where we are*

Sarah rejects our position that CCTV responsibility lies only with drivers. She argues Hopp remains accountable and responsible for informing riders about CCTV under PIPEDA. Meanwhile, Sarah is continuously threatening escalation to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada if her demands (written acknowledgment of non-compliance, commitment to prevent recurrence, and full refund for 3 rides) are not met.

# *Analysis of the righteousness of Sarah’s argument*

Under the Toronto Municipal Code, if a PTC vehicle has a camera, passengers must be notified either: (1) through the platform before booking or (2) via a notice affixed to the vehicle. Sarah claims neither happened. If accurate, this could amount to non-compliance under the Toronto Municipal Code as the PTC licensee. 

# *Next steps* 

We will draft a formal letter to Sarah acknowledging her frustration, clarifying our position on driver-installed cameras, outlining the goodwill refunds (only for 2 rides), and confirming her right to escalate to the OPC.
